body.statement:
The discrete-sine matrix \(U^{\mathrm F}\) belongs to \(\mathbb O_{n,r}\) and satisfies
\[
 \lVert U^{\mathrm F}\rVert_{2,\infty}
 \le\sqrt{\frac{2r}{n+1}}.
\]
Consequently, for every target \(U\) satisfying \(\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}\), the pathwise bound
\[
 \mathcal L(U^{\mathrm F},U)
 \le1+\sqrt{\frac2\mu}
\]
holds.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(x=\pi/(n+1)\).  For integers \(t\) with \(1\le t\le2n\), the geometric-series identity, followed by taking real parts, gives
\[
 C_t:=\sum_{i=1}^n\cos(itx)
 =\frac{\sin(ntx/2)\cos((n+1)tx/2)}{\sin(tx/2)}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The denominator is nonzero because \(0<tx/2<\pi\).  If \(t\) is odd, the cosine in the numerator is \(\cos(t\pi/2)=0\), so \(C_t=0\).  If \(t=2s\) is even, then \(1\le s\le n\), and
\[
 \sin\!\left(\frac{ns\pi}{n+1}\right)
 =\sin\!\left(s\pi-\frac{s\pi}{n+1}\right)
 =(-1)^{s+1}\sin\!\left(\frac{s\pi}{n+1}\right),
\]
while \(\cos(s\pi)=(-1)^s\).  Equation (1) therefore yields \(C_t=-1\).  Also set \(C_0=n\).

For \(1\le k,l\le n\), the product-to-sum identity now gives
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^n\sin(ikx)\sin(ilx)
 =\frac12\{C_{|k-l|}-C_{k+l}\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
When \(k\ne l\), the two indices \(|k-l|\) and \(k+l\) have the same parity and lie between one and \(2n\); the preceding evaluation of \(C_t\) makes the right side of (2) zero.  When \(k=l\), it equals \((C_0-C_{2k})/2=(n+1)/2\).  Multiplication by \(2/(n+1)\) proves that all \(n\) columns of the discrete-sine matrix are orthonormal.  Since \(r\le n\), its first \(r\) columns therefore satisfy
\[
 (U^{\mathrm F})^\top U^{\mathrm F}=I_r,
 \]
which is precisely \(U^{\mathrm F}\in\mathbb O_{n,r}\).

For every row \(i\), \(|\sin(\pi ik/(n+1))|\le1\), so the construction gives
\[
 \lVert e_i^\top U^{\mathrm F}\rVert_2^2
 =\frac2{n+1}\sum_{k=1}^r
 \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi ik}{n+1}\right)
 \le\frac{2r}{n+1}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Taking the maximum over \(i\) proves the first bound.  For the target, \(\mathrm{ass:left\mbox{-}incoherence}\) gives
\(\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}\).  Choosing the admissible alignment \(R=I_r\) in \(\mathrm{def:rowwise\mbox{-}loss}\), applying the rowwise triangle inequality, and then using (3), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal L(U^{\mathrm F},U)
 &\le\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(\lVert U^{\mathrm F}\rVert_{2,\infty}
       +\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\right)\\
 &\le\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(\sqrt{\frac{2r}{n+1}}+sqrt{\frac{\mu r}{n}}\right)\\
 &=1+\sqrt{\frac{2n}{\mu(n+1)}}
 \le1+\sqrt{\frac2\mu}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
All inequalities are deterministic, so the conclusion holds pathwise.
body.justification: The first \(r\) discrete-sine columns give an explicit orthonormal frame with row norm at most \(\sqrt{2r/(n+1)}\).
body.gap: Its loss is only constant order and therefore does not close the minimax rate gap.
body.consumer: It supplies a law-independent safe branch when the IPW radius is noninformative.
